transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in today. What brings you to see me?

Hi, yeah, thanks for seeing me. I mean, I didn't really want to come in, but it's just getting to be this whole thing. I work construction, right? Mostly general labor, hauling materials, that kind of stuff, so I'm on different job sites all day, and I'm here because... well, it's about elevators. 

It sounds so stupid, honestly, because I know they aren't actually dangerous. Like, logically, I know the cables don't just snap, and they have all those emergency brakes and safety inspections and stuff. I've been on sites enough to see how things are built. But whenever I have to get in one—whether it's the temporary hoists on the site or just a regular elevator in a finished building—I just get so incredibly scared. It's this overwhelming feeling like I'm going to be trapped in there, just stuck in this tiny metal box with no way out, and the doors won't open, and nobody will hear me. 

And I just can't make myself feel normal about it. I try to take deep breaths, I try to tell myself it's fine, it's just a short ride and I'll be out in a minute, but my brain just won't listen to reason. It's so frustrating because I’m a tough person, you know? I work hard all day, I work around heavy machinery and scaffolding, but you put me in front of an elevator and I just... I can't shake that trapped feeling. I'll stand there staring at the buttons and just freezing up, which is why I finally decided to come talk to somebody. It's just exhausting having to deal with this every single time I look at a set of sliding doors, and I really just want to be able to ride one like a normal person without feeling like I'm walking into a cage.
Is it only elevators that make you feel this way, or do you also feel anxious in other enclosed or tight spaces, like small rooms, cars, or tunnels?

No, honestly, it's really just the elevators. Which is another reason why it's so weird to me! Like, you'd think if I was scared of being trapped, I'd hate small rooms, right? But I don't. I mean, on the job site, I'm constantly having to squeeze into tight spots. Just last week, my foreman had me clearing out drywall scraps from this tiny, cramped utility closet they were framing out in the basement. There were no windows, barely enough room to even turn around with my tool belt on, and I was totally fine. Not a single drop of sweat. 

And cars? I drive this little two-door coupe, it's tiny, and I sit in rush hour traffic on the highway for like an hour every morning and afternoon. Sometimes my route takes me through that long tunnel downtown, and it's bumper-to-bumper, completely stopped underground. Some of the guys at work complain about feeling boxed in when they get stuck in there, but me? I just turn up the radio and drink my coffee. It doesn't bother me one bit. I can sit in a closet, I can sit in a small car, I can be in a tunnel all day long. 

It's literally just the elevator. It's something about those metal doors sliding shut and knowing I have zero control over the box moving up and down, and that I can't just open a door and walk out if I want to. If it was just about being in a small space, I probably wouldn't even be able to do half the jobs I get assigned on the site, you know? Because construction is full of tight corners. But no, it's just those damn elevators.
